title: Ramayana Crosses ₹1,500 Crore Worldwide in 14 Days, Fifth Indian Film to Reach the Mark
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's epic reached ₹1,519.05 crore worldwide on Day 14 — ₹1,009.05 crore gross in India and ₹510 crore overseas — making Tiwari the only Indian director with two ₹1,500 crore global hits, according to Sacnilk.
body:
• Ramayana crossed ₹1,500 crore worldwide on Day 14, Wednesday, November 18, with a worldwide gross of ₹1,519.05 crore, according to trade tracker Sacnilk.
  • It is only the fifth Indian film ever to cross ₹1,500 crore globally, and the fastest to get there — 14 days, against 16 days for Dhurandhar 2, Filmibeat reported.
  • India gross has also crossed ₹1,000 crore: ₹1,009.05 crore gross and ₹844.40 crore net at home, plus ₹510 crore overseas.
  • Director Nitesh Tiwari is now the only Indian director with two ₹1,500 crore-plus global hits, pairing Ramayana with Dangal (₹2,070 crore).

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana crossed ₹1,500 crore at the worldwide box office on its 14th day in cinemas, becoming only the fifth Indian film to reach that mark and, according to trade tracker Sacnilk, the fastest ever to do it. The Hindi-language epic, released on November 5, collected ₹23.20 crore net in India on Day 14, Wednesday, November 18, across 22,289 shows, The Hollywood Reporter India reported, citing Sacnilk.

The numbers at two weeks

The Day 14 figures take the film's India net to ₹844.40 crore and its India gross to ₹1,009.05 crore — past ₹1,000 crore at home as well. Overseas, the film added ₹8 crore on Day 14, its first day below double digits internationally, taking the overseas total to ₹510 crore and the worldwide gross to ₹1,519.05 crore, according to Sacnilk figures reported by both The Hollywood Reporter India and Filmibeat. The Hollywood Reporter India noted that the overseas run has already set an all-time first-phase international record for an Indian film — a run powered in large part by diaspora audiences.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1zip1rNaNYs

All box-office figures here are trade-tracker estimates compiled by Sacnilk, not studio-audited totals.

The film and its makers

Ramayana is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and stars Ranbir Kapoor as Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Raavan, with Sunny Deol, Ravi Dubey, Arun Govil, Vivek Oberoi, Rakul Preet Singh, Sheeba Chaddha, Adinath Kothare and Lara Dutta in key roles, and a voice performance by Anupam Kher as Jatayu, Filmibeat reported. The pairing of Ranbir Kapoor and Yash on screen for the first time, and their face-off, has been a central draw for audiences.

For Tiwari, the milestone is a personal record. With Ramayana, he has become the only Indian director in history to deliver two ₹1,500 crore-plus global grossers, pairing the new film with his 2016 hit Dangal (₹2,070 crore, including its second-phase China run), The Hollywood Reporter India reported. He is also one of only three Indian directors with multiple ₹1,000 crore global hits, alongside SS Rajamouli and Aditya Dhar.

Where it stands in the all-time list

Only five Indian films have ever crossed ₹1,500 crore worldwide across all release phases, according to Sacnilk: Dangal, Aditya Dhar's Dhurandhar: The Revenge (₹1,813 crore), SS Rajamouli's Baahubali 2: The Conclusion (₹1,788.06 crore), Sukumar's Pushpa 2: The Rule (₹1,742.10 crore), and now Ramayana. Filmibeat reported that Ramayana's 14-day worldwide total of ₹1,519 crore also beat Dhurandhar 2's 14-day collection of ₹1,467.87 crore, and that Dhurandhar 2 had taken 16 days to cross ₹1,500 crore.

What happens next

The film enters Day 15, Thursday, November 19, with advance bookings of ₹12.26 crore gross nationwide including block seats, or ₹8.60 crore excluding block seats, of which the Hindi version contributed ₹5.63 crore, according to Sacnilk's booking report cited by The Hollywood Reporter India. With no major holiday cushion as the film wraps up its second week, Sacnilk projects — as an estimate, not a result — around ₹18–22 crore India net on Day 15. The film is firmly on track, the tracker said, to post Bollywood's third-biggest second week of all time: between November 13 and 18, the Hindi version alone amassed ₹206.50 crore net, already ahead of the full second-week totals of Chhaava (₹180.25 crore), Stree 2 (₹141.40 crore) and Gadar 2 (₹134.47 crore).

Ramayana is playing in cinemas now in India and overseas markets, including North America, where its ₹510 crore international run began with record first-phase collections.
